## 3. Working Hours and Time Conventions

3.1 Standard editorial working hours are 09:00 to 17:30, Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.

3.2 For the purposes of this policy, "business day" means any day from Monday to Friday that is not a public holiday in England and Wales. Where content is scheduled for publication in Scotland or Northern Ireland, the relevant local public holidays shall apply.

3.3 All times stated in this policy are local UK times unless otherwise specified. During British Summer Time (BST), times are one hour ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT). Where a deadline is stated in GMT, it shall be interpreted as BST during the summer period unless the context makes clear otherwise.

3.4 Staff working remotely or travelling abroad must ensure they are aware of the time difference and plan accordingly. It is the responsibility of the individual to confirm the current local time in the UK before submitting work.

3.5 The newsroom operates a reduced service on public holidays. The full list of public holidays is published annually on the intranet and in the production calendar.

## 4. Deadline Types and Definitions

4.1 **Hard deadline:** A deadline that cannot be missed without causing a publication failure or significant disruption. Hard deadlines are identified in the production schedule with the letter "H".

4.2 **Soft deadline:** A deadline that should be met to allow for sub-editing, fact-checking, and design work. Soft deadlines are identified with the letter "S". Missing a soft deadline does not automatically cause a publication failure but may result in the content being reduced in scope or moved to a later edition.

4.3 **Submission deadline:** The time by which a contributor must submit their finished work to the editorial desk. Submission deadlines are always earlier than publication deadlines to allow for review.

4.4 **Publication deadline:** The time by which content must be live on the website or sent to the printer.

**4. Working Hours and Core Availability**

Core production hours are 09:00 to 17:30, Monday to Friday. Staff are expected to be available during these hours for meetings, subbing, and queries.

The digital team operates a shift pattern that includes an early start and a late finish:

- Early shift: 06:00 to 14:00

- Weekend cover: 08:00 to 12:00 on Saturday and Sunday, for the digital bulletin.

Contributors should normally expect to be contacted during core production hours. If a contributor is working in a different time zone, the commissioning editor will agree a contact window in the contributor's local time.

**5. Deadline Submission and Confirmation**

5.1 **Submission.** All copy must be submitted via the content management system (CMS) unless a different method has been agreed in writing. Emailed copy is accepted only with the prior agreement of the production editor.

The Deadline Compliance Policy v3 uses the timezone Europe/London. Record status: current.

5.2 **Confirmation.** The CMS sends an automatic confirmation when copy is submitted. This confirmation is the record of submission time. If a contributor does not receive a confirmation within 15 minutes of submitting, they must contact the production desk.

5.3 **Changing a deadline.** A deadline may be changed only by the production editor or, in their absence, the deputy production editor. Any change must be communicated in writing (email or CMS note) to all affected parties. Verbal agreements to change a deadline are not binding.

5.4 **Disputes.** If a contributor disputes a recorded submission time, the CMS log will be the primary evidence. The production editor will review the log and make a decision within two business days.

**6. Late Submissions**

6.1 **Definition.** A submission is late if it is received after the deadline specified in Section 3 or in a commissioning email.

6.2 **Consequences.** Late submissions may be held for the next edition or bulletin. This decision is at the discretion of the production editor. Repeated lateness may affect future commissioning decisions.

6.3 **Recording.** The production desk records late submissions in the action register, noting the item, the deadline, the actual submission time, and the reason given. This register is reviewed monthly by the head of editorial.

6.4 **Force majeure.** If a submission is late due to a power cut, internet failure, or other event outside the contributor's control, the contributor should inform the production editor as soon as possible. The editor will decide whether to waive the lateness, considering the circumstances and the publication schedule.

**7. Approval and Sign-off**

7.1 **Print edition.** The final page proofs are approved by the editor-in-chief by 18:00 on Wednesday. The production editor is responsible for ensuring that all pages are ready for this approval.
**8. Escalation Procedures**

8.1 **Purpose.** This section sets out the steps to be followed when a deadline is at risk, has been missed, or when there is a disagreement about a submission time. The aim is to resolve issues as quickly as possible and to keep the relevant people informed.

8.2 **Stage 1 – Imminent risk.** If a contributor believes they will not meet a deadline, they must inform the production desk as soon as they become aware of the risk. The production desk will log the warning in the action register. The contributor should also contact their section editor. The production editor will decide whether to reallocate the item, extend the deadline, or make other arrangements.

8.3 **Stage 2 – Missed deadline.** If a submission is late and no warning was given, the production desk will contact the contributor and their section editor. The production desk will record the lateness and the reason given. The section editor is responsible for chasing the item and for keeping the production editor informed of progress.

8.4 **Stage 3 – Dispute.** If a contributor disputes a recorded submission time, the matter is referred to the production editor. The production editor will review the CMS log and make a decision within two business days. If the contributor is not satisfied with the decision, they may ask the head of editorial to review the matter. The head of editorial's decision is final.

8.5 **Stage 4 – Repeated lateness.** If a contributor is late three or more times in any rolling three-month period, the production editor will raise the matter with the head of editorial. The head of editorial will decide whether to issue a written warning or to take other action. This may affect future commissioning decisions.

## 3. Working Hours and Time Conventions

## 4. Deadline Types and Definitions

4.1 **Hard deadline:** A deadline that cannot be missed without causing a publication failure or significant disruption. Hard deadlines are identified in the production schedule with the letter "H".

4.2 **Soft deadline:** A deadline that should be met to allow for sub-editing, fact-checking, and design work. Soft deadlines are identified with the letter "S". Missing a soft deadline does not automatically cause a publication failure but may result in the content being reduced in scope or moved to a later edition.

4.3 **Submission deadline:** The time by which a contributor must submit their finished work to the editorial desk. Submission deadlines are always earlier than publication deadlines to allow for review.

4.4 **Publication deadline:** The time by which content must be live on the website or sent to the printer.

9.4 **Homepage updates:** The homepage is managed by the senior editor on duty. The homepage should be updated throughout the day to reflect the most important stories. 9.5 **Breaking news protocol:** When a major story breaks, the following steps apply:

- The news desk is notified immediately by the reporter or the first journalist to become aware of the story.
- The news desk will assess the story and, if it is confirmed, will issue a "breaking news" alert to the digital team.
- The digital team will prepare a short initial article, which should be published as soon as possible. This initial article should contain only confirmed facts and should be clearly marked as developing.
- The article will be updated as more information becomes available. The on-duty digital producer is responsible for keeping the article up to date and for adding the final version once the story is fully reported.
- If the story is likely to remain ongoing for several hours, a live blog may be started. The decision to start a live blog is made by the news editor in consultation with the digital editor.

9.6 **Content removal and corrections:** If an error is identified in a published article, the following procedure applies:

The Deadline Compliance Policy v3 sets the web_deadline_time to 20:00. Record status: current.

- The error must be reported to the production desk immediately.
- If the error is minor (e.g. a typographical error or a mislabelled image), the production desk will correct the article and log the change.

- The main news story of the day should be shared on all channels within 30 minutes of publication.
- Other stories should be shared at a rate of no more than one per hour per channel, unless the story is of exceptional public interest.
- Social media posts must include a link to the full article on the website. Any post that contains an error must be deleted and reposted with the correction.
- The use of automated scheduling tools is permitted, but the on-duty digital producer must review the scheduled posts at the start of each shift.

9.8 **Video and multimedia:** Video content must be uploaded to the CMS using the standard video upload tool. The following checks must be completed before a video is published:

- The video file must be in the correct format (MP4, H.264 codec).
- The video must have a title, a description, and at least one relevant tag.
- A thumbnail image must be selected. The default thumbnail is not acceptable unless it is manually overridden.
- Closed captions must be added for any video that contains speech. The captions should be checked for accuracy before publication.

If a video fails to upload or is rejected by the CMS, the digital producer should contact the web developer. Videos should not be published via third-party hosting sites unless the video is an embedded piece of content from a provider such as YouTube or Vimeo, in which case the embed code must be checked to ensure it works correctly.
